Where it began

Dasun Shanaka was born in Negombo, on Sri Lanka's west coast, on 9 September 1991. He grew into an all-rounder of the modern kind: a right-arm bowler at a brisk medium pace and a batter built to arrive late in an innings and clear the boundary.

He first played for Sri Lanka in a T20 international in August 2015, and on the tour of England the following summer he made a first-class hundred against Leicestershire.

The player

His Test debut came against England in May 2016, and he made a bright start with the ball, his first wicket being the England captain, Alastair Cook. He finished with 3 for 46 in that match, which stayed his best Test return.

By November 2026 he had played 6 Tests, between 2016 and 2021, taking 13 wickets at 33.15 and scoring 140 runs, with a top score of 66 not out. A month after his Test debut he made a dazzling start in one-day cricket too, taking five wickets against Ireland in his first ODI and being named player of the series. Later came ODI hundreds against Zimbabwe and India.

What made him special

Leadership and a cool head at the end of a chase. He was first given the T20 captaincy in 2019 for a series in Pakistan, and Sri Lanka won all three games, their first whitewash in the format. Formally named T20 captain in 2021, he led them to a first bilateral T20 series win over India that year and, in 2022, to the Asia Cup, the sixth time Sri Lanka had won it.

He also guided the one-day side through the 2023 World Cup Qualifier, where they won all eight games. As a batter, the best example of his finishing came against Australia in June 2022: needing 59 from the last three overs, he went from 6 off 12 balls to a fifty, adding 48 from his next 13, and Sri Lanka won with a ball left. His Test batting was quieter than his white-ball hitting, which may simply be because Test bowlers rarely leave him three overs to win a match in.

Away from the middle

He has been a regular in franchise leagues around the world, from Bangladesh and Pakistan to the Indian Premier League with Gujarat Titans. In 2026 he captained Galle Gallants to their first Lanka Premier League title. Sri Lanka Cricket named him its T20 all-rounder of the year for 2025.

And finally

In July 2026, playing for Seattle Orcas, he took four wickets with the last four balls of a match to win it by nine runs, the first double hat-trick in Major League Cricket. Two months later, in the Caribbean, he made the fastest hundred in CPL history, off 39 balls. Not a bad summer's work.
